Four ways to draw the same fixture

Same match, same crests, same data — four different design philosophies. Each is a genuinely different system, not a re-skin, so the choice is about which voice you want the catalog to have.

All four are rendered live from the real composer path, at the real 800×450 catalog size. Scroll and compare — then tell me the letter.

Current — Minimalist darkas shipped
Philosophy
Modern streaming tile. Near-black gradient, one sport accent, glyph watermark.
Good
Neutral and consistent; plays well in dense grids and dark UIs.
Watch
The direction you're questioning — calm to the point of anonymous.
Cinematic BroadcastExperimental / Ash Thorp
Philosophy
Film-grade lighting. Warm orange and teal volumetrics over a dark base, atmosphere doing the work.
Good for
Highest emotional impact and the most "premium broadcast" of the three. Reads like a promo bumper.
Watch out
Heaviest visually — can compete with the crests. Dark, so it sits well in dark UIs only.
Swiss Tournament PosterMinimalism / Müller-Brockmann
Philosophy
Objectivity as beauty. Flat ink on paper, a mathematical grid, type as the entire graphic.
Good for
Unmistakably a fixture. Type-first means it stays legible at thumbnail size — ideal for dense grids.
Watch out
Light card on dark UIs is a hard contrast jump. Zero atmosphere, so it feels editorial not live.
Dark EditorialMotion poetics / Locomotive
Philosophy
Restraint and air. Near-black, light-weight type, one hairline of muted gold.
Good for
Most elegant and the calmest — never fights the artwork. Scales down beautifully.
Watch out
Quietest of the three; the least immediately "sports". Risk of feeling generic without the accent.

What I'd pick

A if you want the catalog to feel like a broadcast product — it has the most presence and would differentiate you immediately.

B if legibility in a crowded grid matters most — type-first survives the smallest thumbnail.

C if you want quiet, elegant, and future-proof — and are willing to trade some immediacy for it.

Reply with A, B, or C (or a mix — e.g. A's palette with C's restraint) and I'll implement it as the real composer, keep the degradation ladder, and re-verify.
